blocks.etymology: From Middle English warantye, warantie, from Anglo-Norman warrantie, an Old Northern French variant of Old French guarantie (Modern French garantie). Doublet of guarantee and guaranty. More at warrant.

senses.definition: A written agreement promising to repair or replace a product if it breaks within a period.

examples.en: The laptop comes with a two-year warranty.
examples.vi: Chiếc máy tính xách tay đi kèm gói bảo hành hai năm.

examples.en: Is accidental damage covered under the warranty?
examples.vi: Hư hỏng do tai nạn có được bảo hành không?

senses.vi: sự bảo hành; giấy bảo hành

senses.definition: A formal guarantee or promise that certain legal conditions will be met.

examples.en: The contract includes a warranty of quality from the supplier.
examples.vi: Hợp đồng bao gồm sự cam đoan về chất lượng từ nhà cung cấp.

thesaurus.definition: a written assurance that some product or service will be provided or will meet certain specifications

wiktionary.gloss: A guarantee that a certain outcome or obligation will be fulfilled; security.

A legal agreement, either written or oral (an expressed warranty) or implied through the actions of the buyer and seller (an implied warranty), which states that the goods or property in question will be in exactly the same state as promised, such as in a sale of an item or piece of real estate.

examples: I took out an extended warranty on my television for five years at a cost of $100.
I made sure to check the terms of my warranty for my computer to ensure that I was covered in case it broke down.
wiktionary.gloss: A written guarantee, usually over a fixed period, provided to someone who buys a product or item, which states that certain repairs and/or replacement parts will be provided free of charge in case of damage or a defect.
A stipulation of an insurance policy made by an insuree, guaranteeing that the facts of the policy are true and the insurance risk is as stated, which if not fulfilled renders the policy void.
Justification or mandate to do something, especially in terms of one’s personal conduct; warrant.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English warantye, warantie, from Anglo-Norman warrantie, an Old Northern French variant of Old French guarantie (Modern French garantie). Doublet of guarantee and guaranty. More at warrant.

wiktionary.gloss: To warrant; to guarantee.
